surfaces.reason: The installer merges a bounded Clade-managed block into ~/.codex/AGENTS.md without replacing user-authored guidance.
Developer workflows are selected by plugins/clade/skills.list and generated with Codex-native paths and tool semantics.
Codex ships two bounded profiles with explicit sandbox, ownership, verifier, and no-recursion contracts instead of copying Claude agent prompts.
Only session context and destructive-command protection have native Codex event and trust semantics; Claude-only lifecycle hooks stay excluded.
Codex has no distributable equivalent of Claude system-prompt output styles, so their evidence and response-register invariants are adapted as durable guidance.
Model, trust, permission, MCP authentication, and personal plugin controls remain user-scoped config.toml state and are never overwritten by the repository installer.
The MCP bridge is for external clients; installing it inside Codex beside the native plugin duplicates skills and creates nested Codex sessions.

skill_exclusions.reason: Large marketing suites stay available through the Claude framework and MCP catalog; loading them into the developer-focused Codex plugin would create discovery noise.
These workflows depend on Claude Workflow, Stop-hook, job-registry, or cross-runtime launch semantics and require a separate native design.
These workflows mutate or interpret Claude-specific installation, hook, correction, profile, skill-authoring, or status-line state.
Native frontend-design, review, verify, and delivery workflows cover the supported behavior without carrying a second overlapping command.
These specialized or provider-specific workflows remain opt-in through Claude or MCP until a Codex-native product use case justifies plugin discovery cost.
